title: Earnings week ahead: MSFT, AAPL, GOOG, AMZN, META, XOM, CVX, KO, V, SBUX, F, GM, and more
content:
[Magnifying Glass On Top Of Bar Chart Showing Decling Performance]
DNY59/iStock via Getty Images

As earnings season hits its peak, the week ahead stands out as one of the most consequential reporting stretches of the year.

Five members of the Magnificent Seven, Apple (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL]), Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]), and Meta (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), headline the calendar, placing a sharp spotlight on AI monetization, cloud demand, digital advertising, and consumer ecosystems.

Beyond big tech, the week spans a remarkably broad cross-section of the global economy.

Energy majors Exxon Mobil (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]), Chevron (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX]), and ConocoPhillips (COP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/COP]) will reflect commodity dynamics, while industrial bellwethers Caterpillar (CAT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CAT]), General Dynamics (GD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GD]), and UPS offer a read on infrastructure, defense, and global logistics demand.

Consumer and payments giants like Coca-Cola (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]), Starbucks (SBUX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SBUX]), Chipotle (CMG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CMG]), Visa (V [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/V]), and Mastercard (MA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MA]) will provide cues on spending resilience, and healthcare leaders Eli Lilly (LLY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LLY]), Merck (MRK [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MRK]), AbbVie (ABBV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ABBV]), and Amgen (AMGN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMGN]) will highlight innovation pipelines and demand durability.

The calendar further extends into autos, telecom, fintech, and emerging tech, with Ford (F [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/F]), GM, T-Mobile (TMUS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TMUS]), Verizon (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]), Robinhood (HOOD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HOOD]), Roku (ROKU [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ROKU]), and Enphase Energy (ENPH [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ENPH]) adding depth across connectivity, retail investing, and clean energy.

Rounding out the week are names spanning digital platforms, materials, and semiconductors, including QUALCOMM (QCOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/QCOM]), Spotify (SPOT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SPOT]), Booking Holdings (BKNG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BKNG]), First Solar (FSLR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/FSLR]), and Vale (VALE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VALE]).

With leadership stocks and cyclical sectors reporting side by side, this week's earnings will deliver one of the most comprehensive snapshots yet of global growth, corporate spending, and market direction, and a critical test of whether elevated expectations around AI, consumption, and macro resilience can hold.

Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of April 20 to April 24:

MONDAY, APRIL 27

VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ])

Verizon Communications (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]) is set to report Q1 results before Monday’s open, with analysts expecting modest Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system remains more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing limited growth visibility.

SA VIEWS REMAIN MIXED:

Kenio Fontes recently downgraded the stock to Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891357-verizon-why-shareholders-should-fear-the-amazon-flywheel-downgrade], pointing to modest near-term momentum (2–3% revenue growth and 4–5% EPS guidance for 2026) amid intense competition from T-Mobile US and AT&T.

On the bullish side, The Alpha Analyst reiterates a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891143-verizon-stock-strong-buy-resilient-cash-flow-stable-valuation], viewing VZ as an income-focused play supported by resilient cash flows, ~9x forward earnings valuation, and robust capital return plans. Management’s focus on ~$5B in cost savings, disciplined capex, and steady free cash flow growth underpins dividend sustainability and buybacks.

In contrast, SA Investing Group Leader Stone Fox Capital maintains a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891802-verizon-path-back-down-to-40], citing structural growth challenges, high leverage, and limited exposure to next-generation growth areas. Despite its ~6% yield, concerns around flat wireless growth and reliance on legacy assets could pressure long-term valuation.

 	* Consensus EPS Estimates: $1.21
 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: $34.86B
 	* Earnings Insight: The company has exceeded EPS expectations in all the past 8 quarters and revenue estimates 50% of the time in that span.

ALSO REPORTING: Nucor (NUE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NUE]), Ventas (VTR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VTR]), Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BBBY]), NOV (NOV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NOV]), Domino's Pizza (DPZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/DPZ]), Public Storage (PSA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PSA]), AvalonBay Communities (AVB [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AVB]), Cadence Design Systems (CDNS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CDNS]), Lending Club (LC [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LC]), Alliance Resource Partners (ARLP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ARLP]), Noble Corporation (NE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NE]), Easterly Government Properties (DEA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/DEA]), and more.

TUESDAY, APRIL 28

COCA-COLA (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO])

The Coca-Cola Company (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]) is set to report Q1 results before Tuesday’s open, with analysts expecting over 9% Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

The company recently announced a $1B investment [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4571064-coca-cola-unveils-1b-south-africa-investment-plan-through-2030] in South Africa through 2030, alongside local bottling partners, aimed at expanding production, strengthening distribution, and driving product innovation, highlighting its asset-light, franchise-driven model.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system is more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

SA author YR Research reiterates a Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890277-coca-cola-the-retirement-dream], emphasizing Coca-Cola’s defensive appeal, consistent mid-single-digit organic growth, and strong dividend profile, with expected annual returns of 8–10%.

In contrast, SA Investing Group Leader Dhierin Bechai downgraded the stock to Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890598-coca-cola-buy-for-the-dividend-hold-for-the-upside-downgrade], noting limited upside after recent outperformance, with a price target implying modest gains despite stable cash flows and resilient fundamentals.

 	* Consensus EPS Estimates: $0.81
 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: $12.24B
 	* Earnings Insight: The beverage giant has beaten EPS expectations in 8 straight quarters and revenue in 7 of those reports.

WEDNESDAY, APRIL 29

MICROSOFT CORPORATION (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), AMAZON.COM (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), META PLATFORMS (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), AND ALPHABET (GOOG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOG])

Wednesday shapes up as a pivotal moment for Big Tech, with four “Magnificent 7” names. Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Meta Platforms (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), and Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]) are all set to report after the market closes, placing the spotlight firmly on AI, cloud, and digital advertising trends.

Heading into earnings, the narrative remains centered [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4576930-the-earnings-tightrope-will-mag-7-bulls-pivot-to-bottom-fishing] on AI-driven growth versus margin pressure. Microsoft’s Azure momentum is key, though rising CapEx continues to divide opinion. Meta is viewed constructively on pullbacks despite mixed reception to recent AI developments, while Alphabet’s steady growth is tempered by heavy investments in AI and adjacent ventures. Amazon, meanwhile, is doubling down on AI and infrastructure through its massive AWS investments, with markets closely watching returns on capital.

Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy across all four names, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system takes a more measured stance with Hold ratings, reflecting valuation concerns.

However, SA author Gary Alexander rates Amazon a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4893417-amazon-sell-on-anthropic-deal-spike-valuation-doesnt-add-up], arguing its ~$2.7T valuation is difficult to justify despite recent momentum driven by AWS and AI partnerships.

Similarly, Dmytro Lebid sees Microsoft as a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891641-microsoft-don-t-buy-the-dip-a-30-percent-correction-is-still-ahead], citing rising capital intensity, margin pressure, and potential multiple compression as the business shifts toward infrastructure-heavy AI investments.

Here’s a preview of the key information ahead of the reports: [https://static.seekingalpha.com/uploads/2026/4/24/saupload_MAG7.png]

ALSO REPORTING: Google (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]), Ford Motor (F [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/F]), AbbVie (ABBV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ABBV]), Qualcomm (QCOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/QCOM]), Teladoc Health (TDOC [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TDOC]), SoFi (SOFI [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SOFI]), Teva Pharmaceutical Industries (TEVA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TEVA]), Etsy (ETSY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ETSY]), GlaxoSmithKline (GSK [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GSK]), Phillips 66 (PSX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PSX]), Biogen (BIIB [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BIIB]), Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CMG]), AstraZeneca (AZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AZN]), Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/REGN]), Sundial Growers (SNDL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SNDL]), Lemonade (LMND [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LMND]), General Dynamics (GD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GD]), eBay (EBAY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/EBAY]), and more.

THURSDAY, APRIL 30

APPLE (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL])

California-based Apple (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL]), another core member of the “Magnificent Seven,” is set to report FQ2 results after Thursday’s close, with analysts expecting ~18% Y/Y EPS growth on ~15% revenue expansion.

Recent developments have kept the spotlight on the iPhone maker. A major leadership transition is underway, with Tim Cook set to move into an Executive Chairman role and John Ternus stepping in as CEO, signaling a stronger product and engineering focus.

Meanwhile, iPhone shipments in China rose 20% in Q1, supported by the latest iPhone cycle, pricing actions, and government incentives.

Wall Street remains bullish, with Morgan Stanley viewing the upcoming print as a potential “clearing event,” driven by solid momentum across iPhone, Mac, and Services.

However, Seeking Alpha’s Quant Rating stays at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

SA views are notably divided.

Louis Gerard rates the stock a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892801-apple-the-ceo-transition-is-a-multiple-compression-catalyst], flagging elevated multiples, AI execution risks, and potential margin pressure, while Given Mahlangu maintains a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892654-apple-stock-see-an-alchain-allen-theorem-at-play-upgrade-strong-buy], pointing to Apple’s pricing advantage and resilient demand dynamics.

Bill Maurer adopts a wait-and-watch [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892392-apple-enters-new-leadership-era] stance, highlighting strong fundamentals but cautioning that premium valuation may limit near-term upside.

 	* Consensus EPS Estimates: $1.95
 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: $109.69B
 	* Earnings Insight: Apple has beaten EPS and revenue expectations in 8 straight quarters.

ALSO REPORTING: Altria Group (MO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MO]), Merck & Co. FRIDAY, MAY 1

EXXON MOBIL (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]) AND CHEVRON (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX])

Chevron Corporation (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX]) and Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]) are all set to report Q1 results before Friday’s open, with analysts expecting a mixed performance amid a volatile energy backdrop.

Recent developments highlight diverging narratives. Exxon has advanced its LNG ambitions, with its Golden Pass project [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578804-exxon-qatarenergy-ship-first-lng-cargo-from-golden-pass-export-terminal] shipping its first cargo, while also exploring downstream portfolio optimization, including a potential sale of its Hong Kong retail network. However, Wolfe Research recently downgraded the stock, citing valuation concerns after its strong run.

Chevron, meanwhile, has resumed [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578829-chevron-resumes-full-production-at-wheatstone-lng-after-cyclone-damage-shutdown] full production at its Wheatstone LNG facility following outage-related disruptions, though operational challenges, including a refinery incident in Texas, could weigh on near-term downstream performance.

Sentiment remains broadly constructive. Wall Street maintains Buy ratings on both names, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system assigns Strong Buy ratings [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], supported by elevated oil prices and geopolitical tailwinds.

SA author views reflect this divergence. Asian Value Investor maintains a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4889690-chevron-stock-growth-drivers-are-in-sync-with-valuation-and-technicals] on Chevron, citing its upstream leverage, strong balance sheet, and resilience to higher oil prices. In contrast, Exxon is rated Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4889477-exxon-mobil-stock-price-drop-priced-in-everything-but-didnt-deeply-discount-it], with solid fundamentals largely priced in and technical indicators signaling caution despite continued operational strength.

 	* Consensus EPS Estimates: XOM: $1.0; CVX: $1.0
 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: XOM: $85.26B; CVX: $52.70B
 	* Earnings Insight: XOM has topped EPS expectations in 7 of the past 8 quarters, beating revenue estimates in 6 of those reports, whereas CVX has beaten EPS in 6 and revenue estimates in 5 of those reports.

title: Insider trades: Morgan Stanley, Uber, Adobe among notable names
content:
[Adobe headquarters in San Jose, California, USA]
JHVEPhoto

This week insider trades were seen across major firms like Uber (UBER [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/UBER]) and Morgan Stanley (MS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MS]). The following transactions occurred between April 20, 2026, and April 24, 2026.

Morgan Stanley (MS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MS]) Chief Legal and Administrative Officer Eric Grossman sold 11,118 shares at a price range of $190 to $191.5 per share for a total value of $2.12M, reducing his direct holdings by 6.16% to 169,403 shares.

Adobe (ADBE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ADBE]) EVP and CFO Daniel Durn disposed of 3.02% of his direct holdings in the firm. He sold 1,336 shares at $248.02 per share for $331,355, trimming his stake to 42,833 shares.

Tilray Brands (TLRY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TLRY]) director David Hopkinson sold 33,556 shares at $6.94 per share for $232,879, fully exiting his direct position.

U.S. Bancorp (USB [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/USB]) Vice Chair Jodi Richard sold 40,000 shares, reducing her direct holdings by 16.18%. She sold each share at $57.00, totaling $2.28M and reducing her stake to 207,251 shares.

Fluor Corp. disposed of 13.5M shares of NuScale Power (SMR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SMR]) at $11.81 each for proceeds of $159.4 million, completely exiting its stake in the company.

On the purchase side, Uber (UBER [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/UBER]) revealed that its holdings in EV maker Lucid have increased to 37.75M shares, representing an 11.52% stake in the company. It holds the stake indirectly through its wholly owned subsidiary, SMB Holding Corporation.

Vladimir Galkin revealed in a filing that he holds 37.2M shares of JetBlue (JBLU [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/JBLU]), translating to a 10% stake in the firm.

Baozun (BZUN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BZUN]) CEO Wenbin Qiu purchased 16,000 shares of the company for $3.14 each for a total value of $50,240. The CEO’s indirect holdings have risen to 1.43M shares.

Together, these funding moves, transatlantic growth, and pricing-practice questions highlight how JetBlue is balancing liquidity needs, international expansion, and reputational risk. We’ll now examine how JetBlue’s new US$500 million aircraft-backed financing commitment could influence its investment narrative and future risk profile.

To own JetBlue, you need to believe its turnaround can offset recent losses and competitive pressures, with the key near term catalyst being evidence that network changes and partnerships are lifting revenue quality. The biggest risk remains pressure on margins from fuel, labor, and intense fare competition. The new US$500 million aircraft backed facility and Boston Europe growth help liquidity and relevance, but do not fundamentally change that risk reward balance on their own.

title: Why Spirit's crisis benefits Frontier and JetBlue
content:
Spirit Airlines (FLYQQ) has been in trouble long before the war-driven oil price spike. But now, fuel prices might dictate the carrier’s survival.

According to JPMorgan analyst Jamie Baker, if gas prices hit $4.60 a gallon, Spirit could face $360 million in additional expenses. That figure exceeds the airline’s total year-end cash balance of $337 million.

The result could be liquidation. CNBC reported that a shutdown could come as soon as this week. To stave it off, Spirit has reportedly offered the US government an equity stake in exchange for emergency funding. The Wall Street Journal reported that the carrier may be close to a $500 million rescue package from the Trump administration.

“Spirit’s in a tough spot,” SDT Capital Advisors president Steve Trent told Yahoo Finance.

Wall Street is already reacting. Earlier this week, President Trump claimed he’d “love somebody to buy Spirit,” prompting the stock to jump 100%. Spirit stock then catapulted over 600% just a day later as investors bet that a federal lifeline could open the door to a merger. However, the volatility remains extreme, as shares have dropped over 80% in the last year.

Read more: $100 oil could send airfare soaring this summer. These tips could save you.

Analysts remain skeptical of government-led rescue. “We’re concerned,” Baker said, suggesting that if Spirit receives a federal boost, rivals like JetBlue (JBLU) and Frontier (ULCC) may be inclined to follow suit.

“Truthfully, we can think of no greater defiant gesture towards the likes of Delta (DAL) and United (UAL) than the government stepping in with lopsided assistance,” Baker said.A Spirit Airlines plane taxis at Hollywood Burbank Airport on April 16, 2026, in Burbank, California. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)·Justin Sullivan via Getty Images

Spirit has been struggling for years. High debt and operational costs were exacerbated by shifting consumer demand. The ultralow-cost model dwindled as travelers opted for carriers offering better perks at similar prices. Spirit was caught in the middle: too expensive to be the cheapest, but too basic to be the best.

The bleeding hasn’t stopped. The company has filed for bankruptcy twice, most recently last August. It posted a net loss of $2.7 billion in 2025, up significantly from the $1.2 billion the company posted in 2024. A massive engine recall further grounded dozens of its aircraft.

Read more: Find the best travel credit cards for April 2026

Today, investors are left wondering which carrier wins if Spirit vanishes.

In a note to clients, Raymond James analyst Savanthi Syth described the timing of these liquidation reports as “unsurprising” given the industry’s post-holiday lull. She noted that because Spirit’s customers tend to book flights at the last minute, the airline lacks advanced ticket sales. Rival airlines can use the cash from future summer bookings to bridge the gap during seasonal slowdowns.

Story Continues

Spirit’s yellow planes are already becoming less common at major hubs. Earlier this year, United agreed to purchase Spirit’s final two designated gates at Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport for approximately $30.2 million.

Simultaneously, United, JetBlue, and Frontier are aggressively adding flights to Spirit’s most profitable hubs, like Fort Lauderdale and Orlando. For the upcoming quarter, Spirit only holds 2% of scheduled flights — a signal that rising fuel costs are forcing the carrier to cut routes. By year’s end, Syth noted Spirit will dwindle to just 80 aircraft.

“We believe JetBlue and Frontier would be the largest beneficiaries of a Spirit liquidation,” Syth said.

JetBlue — which agreed to acquire Spirit for $3.8 billion in 2022 — has now replaced Frontier as Spirit’s primary overlap, according to Syth.

As legacy airlines widen the gap over low-cost carriers, JPMorgan noted that trends will continue to favor the industry’s “Big 3”: Delta, United, and American Airlines (AAL).

The firm remains Overweight on the trio. Delta has “reclaimed the throne” by leaning into robust demand for premium products that JPMorgan expects to continue for the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, United’s strategy is to capitalize on a surge in business and international travel, and American’s international exposure stands to gain even more momentum.Spirit Airlines baggage tags are seen near a check-in counter at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport on November 13, 2024, in Austin, Texas.(Brandon Bell/Getty Images)·Brandon Bell via Getty Images

title: Lawsuit accuses JetBlue of using customers' personal data to raise air fares
content:
By Jonathan Stempel

NEW YORK, April 23 (Reuters) - JetBlue has been sued in a proposed class action claiming it uses customers' personal data to ‌set ticket prices, after its response to a social media post raised ‌concern that the carrier employed "surveillance pricing" to make flying more expensive.

According to a complaint filed late Wednesday ​in Brooklyn federal court, JetBlue conceals its use of "trackers" to set prices dynamically, and shares data with third parties whose programs help it decide when to raise fares.

"Consumers should not have to have their privacy rights violated to participate in [JetBlue's] digital rat race ‌for airline tickets which should ⁠cost the same for each similarly seated passenger," the plaintiff, Andrew Phillips, said in the complaint.

JetBlue declined to comment on the ⁠lawsuit on Thursday. It also said it does not use personal data or artificial intelligence to set ticket prices.

Surveillance pricing lets companies use browsing histories, locations and other personal ​data to ​set individual prices.

The lawsuit followed an April ​18 exchange on X where ‌a passenger praised JetBlue but said "a $230 increase on a ticket after one day is crazy. I'm just trying to make it to a funeral."

JetBlue's response said the passenger should try "clearing your cache and cookies or booking with an incognito window. We're sorry for your loss."

The Long Island City, New York-based carrier said on Monday its ‌response was incorrect, while adding that "fares can change ​at any moment as seats are purchased or ​as inventory is adjusted based on ​demand."

On Tuesday, two Democratic lawmakers in Congress asked JetBlue to ‌respond to detailed questions about pricing, including ​whether it uses ​personal data "to inform prices."

In November, two dozen congressional lawmakers asked Delta Air Lines to address whether it used or plans to use generative AI in ​setting prices. Delta said no.

Phillips' ‌lawsuit seeks unspecified damages for JetBlue's alleged violations of a federal anti-wiretapping ​law and New York state consumer protection laws.

(Reporting by Jonathan Stempel ​in New York, Editing by Louise Heavens)

title: JetBlue hit with surveillance accusations after a tweet to disgruntled customer goes wrong
content:
In the past, when you booked a plane ticket or ordered food for delivery, you could be confident that the price you were paying or the deal you were offered were the same for every other customer.

But there have been more and more cases where this is not what's actually happening, as individuals are sometimes paying more (or less) for the same thing. On April 18, a JetBlue (NASDAQ: JBLU) customer took to X to express their frustration with the airline's pricing.

"I love flying JetBlue but a $230 increase on a ticket after one day is crazy," the customer shared (1). "I'm just trying to make it to a funeral."

JetBlue's official X account replied with a controversial post that has since been deleted.

"Try clearing your cache and cookies or booking with an incognito window," JetBlue's account advised (2). "We're sorry for your loss."

That thread quickly went viral, with consumer advocates claiming the JetBlue response showed how airlines use your personal data to adjust pricing (3). JetBlue promptly deleted the reply post and called it an employee error, but as MarketWatch reports, "the internet flagged the response as a quiet admission of surveillance pricing."

A JetBlue spokesperson has since apologized for the error in an email to MarketWatch, saying the airline's fares "are not determined by cached data or other personal information."

By April 22, a post on X from Reclaim The Net — which features a screengrab of the original customer's post, as well as JetBlue's reply — had more than five million views and around 9,000 reposts.

"Did JetBlue just admit to surveillance pricing?" Reclaim The Net pondered in its post.

Emerita Torres, a New York State Assemblymember, added her voice to this debate on X (4), claiming "Surveillance pricing is REAL and JetBlue just admitted it. Our web searches, mouse clicks and other forms of our personal data should not be used against us."

Greg Casar, a Congressman in Texas, also piped up on X (5), saying "You deserve to know if airlines are collecting your personal information and using it in any way to set prices."

Story Continues

This viral JetBlue story is the latest example in a slew of cases about surveillance pricing, and it's important for consumers to be aware of this practice and approach their purchases with a critical eye.

What is surveillance pricing?

Reuters (6) describes surveillance pricing as "a strategy where ‌companies ⁠use a consumer's personal data — such as browsing history, location and shopping habits — to set individualized, algorithmic prices for products, as opposed to using standard, market-wide pricing."

In other words, the price you see (and pay) when shopping online may be different than someone else buying the same item from the same retailer.

Business Insider conducted its own surveillance pricing experiment in March by having several employees order a McDonald's Big Mac meal with medium fries and a drink. These orders were made at the same time and were delivered via Uber Eats from the same McDonald's location to BI's office in Manhattan (7).

The result? None of the employees paid the same amount, with totals varying by 15 to 20 cents — the difference was reportedly found in the Uber service fee.

Retailers using artificial intelligence to assist with surveillance pricing now have the ability to "personalize consumer interactions to potentially deepen engagement, loyalty and customer delight," as reported by Forbes (8). But at a glance, it looks as though some of the prices we pay are now designed to benefit the retailer and no longer maintain a consistent sticker price that you would have paid in the past.

Read More: This $1B private real estate fund is now accessible to non-millionaires. Start investing with just $10

What is being done about it?

Lindsay Owens, executive director of the think tank Groundwork Collaborative, shared her thoughts with MarketWatch (9), stating that "While JetBlue is now claiming the post was an 'error,' their only mistake was pulling back the curtain on their own deceptive pricing practices."

In December 2025, Groundwork Collaborative, Consumer Reports and More Perfect Union published a joint investigation into Instacart's pricing tactics, which discovered a price variation of up to 23% per item even when customers bought the same thing from the same store at the same time (10) — just like Business Insider discovered with the Big Macs.

Soon after the investigation went public, Instacart revealed it would end the program it was testing that gave customers different prices for the same item.

Back in January 2025, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) released a surveillance pricing market study which found that personal details often are used to customize a price for the same good or service (11).

"Initial staff findings show that retailers frequently use people's personal information to set targeted, tailored prices for goods and services — from a person's location and demographics, down to their mouse movements on a webpage," said Linda M. Khan, who was the FTC chair at the time.

According to MarketWatch, some states have started taking action to try and stop surveillance pricing practices (12). The Protection from Predatory Pricing Act was just passed in Maryland's legislature and if it's signed into law, it will be the first state law specifically targeting surveillance pricing.

Furthermore, the state of New York now requires retailers to disclose when their prices are set using personal data, and Assemblymember Torres recently introduced the One Fair Price Act aimed at banning surveillance pricing in the state.

It's encouraging to see that some of those in power, along with the FTC, are taking surveillance pricing seriously, because even if the price differences aren't significant, small increases in cost per item can add up over a week, month, and year for a family.
